skill.name: entra-app-registration
skill.description: Guides Microsoft Entra ID app registration, OAuth flows, API permissions, Azure CLI setup, Bicep examples, and MSAL integration.
skill.summary: Create and troubleshoot Microsoft Entra app registrations with OAuth, API permissions, and MSAL guidance.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Static analysis produced many alerts, but review found they are mostly Markdown examples for Microsoft Entra, OAuth, Azure CLI, and SDK usage. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden execution was found. The main residual risk is that privileged Azure CLI examples can modify a tenant if an agent or user runs them without review.

remediation.issue: Privileged Azure CLI examples can change tenant state.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear confirmation guidance before credential reset, admin consent, owner change, and delete commands.

remediation.issue: Examples include client secrets and certificate workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholders only, remind users not to paste secrets, and prefer managed identity or Key Vault.

remediation.issue: Cleanup examples can delete app registrations.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to verify tenant, filters, and target app IDs before running cleanup commands.

content.value_statement: Microsoft Entra app registration work spans portal settings, OAuth flows, API permissions, and SDK setup. This skill gives structured guidance for secure Microsoft identity integration.
actual_capabilities: Explains app registration concepts, identifiers, redirect URIs, service principals, and supported account types.
Guides first-time app registration setup with portal steps and Azure CLI examples.
Describes authorization code, client credentials, device code, and implicit OAuth flow patterns.
Maps delegated and application Microsoft Graph permissions to consent and least-privilege choices.
Provides MSAL console app examples and Azure identity SDK quick references.
Helps troubleshoot redirect URI, consent, token, client secret, and configuration errors.
limitations: It does not verify live tenant state unless connected tooling provides that data.
It cannot grant consent, create secrets, or change Azure resources without separate execution.
Examples must be adapted to each tenant, app type, and security policy.
It is not a replacement for identity governance or compliance review.

use_cases.title: Create a first app registration
use_cases.description: Choose app type, configure redirect URIs, capture client IDs, and add initial Microsoft Graph permissions.

use_cases.title: Standardize service authentication
use_cases.description: Plan client credentials flow, service principal setup, certificate use, and least-privilege application permissions.

use_cases.title: Diagnose sign-in failures
use_cases.description: Trace redirect URI mismatches, missing consent, token claim issues, and invalid client secret errors.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a new registration
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a Microsoft Entra app registration for a web application. Ask for the required details before suggesting settings.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Graph permissions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my app requirements and recommend delegated or application Microsoft Graph permissions with least privilege.

prompt_templates.title: Implement an OAuth flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the OAuth 2.0 flow and MSAL setup for a console app that signs in users and calls Microsoft Graph.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and troubleshoot configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Entra app registration configuration and identify redirect URI, consent, secret, token, and tenant risks.

output_examples.input: I need a single-tenant web app registration for an internal dashboard.
output: Use accounts in this organizational directory only.
Register web redirect URIs exactly as used by the application.
Use authorization code flow with MSAL.
Request only the Microsoft Graph scopes required by the dashboard.

output_examples.input: My app fails with AADSTS50011 after sign-in.
output: Compare the request redirect URI with the registered URI exactly.
Check scheme, host casing, path, trailing slash, port, and platform type.
Update the app registration or application configuration so the values match.

output_examples.input: A background service must call Microsoft Graph without a user.
output: Use client credentials flow with application permissions.
Prefer certificate or managed identity where possible.
Grant admin consent only for minimal required permissions.
Rotate credentials and monitor service principal sign-ins.

best_practices: Confirm tenant, app ID, and redirect URI values before running Azure CLI commands.
Use least-privilege permissions and document why each permission is required.
Store secrets in managed identity, Key Vault, or secure environment configuration.
anti_patterns: Granting broad application permissions before validating the business requirement.
Copying real client secrets or tenant IDs into shared prompts or tickets.
Running cleanup or credential reset commands against production without a rollback plan.

faq.question: Can this skill create an app registration for me?
faq.answer: It can guide the steps and provide commands. Execution requires separate Azure access and user approval.

faq.question: Does it support Azure AD terminology?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Microsoft Entra ID and references Azure AD where tools still use that name.

faq.question: Can it help choose permission types?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains delegated and application permissions and recommends least-privilege choices.

faq.question: Does it include MSAL examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes console app examples and SDK quick references for common Microsoft identity libraries.

faq.question: Is it safe to paste real client secrets into prompts?
faq.answer: No. Use placeholders in prompts and keep real secrets in approved secret stores.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot AADSTS errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers common redirect URI, consent, tenant, client secret, and token errors.
